pr_title: Fix incorrect metadata token written for array, pointer populated from TypeBuilder
pr_body:
When array or pointer type created from `TypeBuilder` instance and referenced in IL `ILGenerator` writes incorrect/default token when it should reserve the token and fill in on assembly save. Fix the issue, for array and pointer types, looks ByRef types do not need to be covered.

Fixes https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/issues/102687
pr_comments:
> looks ByRef types do not need to be covered.

Why not? `ldtoken MyType&` is valid IL.

> Why not? ldtoken MyType& is valid IL.

Was not sure it could be used, thanks!

issue_context.title: PersistedAssemblyBuilder writes corrupt metadata tokens to IL stream for arrays of newly-declared types
comments:
Tagging subscribers to this area: @dotnet/area-system-reflection-emit
See info in [area-owners.md](https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/blob/main/docs/area-owners.md) if you want to be subscribed.
<!-- Policy app identification https://img.shields.io/static/v1?label=PullRequestIssueManagement. -->

This error does not occur for arrays of external types.  For example, if I change the type in the `IsInst` line to `typeof(int[])` or `typeof(PersistedAssemblyBuilder[])`, everything executes as expected.  But it appears that any type token for an array of a type declared within the `PersistedAssemblyBuilder` will be corrupted in this way.

review_comments:
This is invalid IL. The method should either return `object` instead of bool; or there needs to be `ldnull` + `cgt.un` here to convert the object to bool.

Once this is fixed, I expect that the test is going to pass on Mono.

Sorry, that's on me.  That was copied directly from my original test; I wrote that intuitively (an "is instance" opcode feels like it should be an `is`, not an `as`) rather than looking up the formal specification.  Good catch!
